$provenance: Vendored from https://github.com/appsecco/dvna (Damn Vulnerable NodeJS Application, MIT license) at pinned commit 9ba473add536f66ac9007966acb2a775dd31277 (2023-11-08). Trimmed to the security-relevant Express/Sequelize source (config/, core/, models/, routes/, server.js, package.json) — views/, public/, docs/, docker files dropped as not relevant to static analysis. Every finding below was hand-verified by reading this exact vendored source (see corpus/README.md for the sampling method). Do not "fix" these — they are the labels the precision/recall gate scores against.

expectedFindings.description: userSearch handler string-concatenates untrusted `req.body.login` into a raw SQL string and runs it via `db.sequelize.query()` (classic SQLi, DVNA's OWASP A1 lab).
ping handler concatenates untrusted `req.body.address` directly into a shell command passed to `child_process.exec()` (OS command injection).
`redirect` handler calls `res.redirect(req.query.url)` with the destination taken directly from an unvalidated query parameter (open redirect, DVNA's unvalidated-redirect lab).

bulkProductsLegacy passes an uploaded file's raw bytes straight to `node-serialize`'s `unserialize()` — the well-known node-serialize gadget (CVE-2017-5941 class) allows arbitrary code execution via a crafted `_$$ND_FUNC$$_` payload.
bulkProducts parses an uploaded XML file with `libxmljs.parseXmlString(..., {noent: true})` — `noent: true` explicitly enables external general-entity expansion on untrusted input (XXE).

Password-reset token is `md5(login)` — a deterministic, unsalted hash of a public value, so any reset token is trivially guessable/computable from the username alone (weak/broken token scheme built on MD5).
`/admin/usersapi` is gated only by `isAuthenticated` (any logged-in user), never by `req.user.role === 'admin'` — missing function-level access control on an admin-only endpoint.

listUsersAPI (reachable via the broken-access-control endpoint above) serializes full Sequelize `User` records — including the `password` hash column (models/user.js) — into the JSON response with no attribute exclusion.
